mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2.5% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during rising rate periods (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not cross the threshold in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 3.5% predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor market disengagement reduces corporate optimism.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >50% of months with UNRATE > 3.5%, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly HOUST (household spending index) exceeds 1250 for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver a positive 20-day forward return as strong consumer demand supports corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 1250 for two consecutive months ending prior to decision
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during qualifying periods (p > 0.05), or the two-month streak does not precede the window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 5% predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak manufacturing output signals economic weakness.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly decline > 5% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during INDPRO declines >5%, or the effect is not statistically robust (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of FEDFUNDS below 2% and CPIAUCSL above 253 imply a deflationary bias that drives a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors price in lower future inflation risk.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% for two consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL > 253 in the same months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during qualifying dual regime (p > 0.05), or proxies fail to co-occur as specified.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in PAYEMS (employment months) below 150,000 triggers a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates labor market tightening.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative when PAYEMS falls below threshold (p > 0.05), or the signal is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (GDP) grows by over 3% in the quarter ending three months prior, the S&P 500 is expected to post a positive 20-day forward return reflecting optimism about economic expansion.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth > 3% in the quarter three months prior
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during qualifying GDP growth (p > 0.05), or the trigger is not met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 4-month decline in RSAFS (retail sales) below 500,000 suggests weak consumer demand, resulting in a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 500,000 for four consecutive months ending prior to decision
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative during the four-month streak (p > 0.05), or the streak does not precede the window.
